Rashi on Shabbat 69a:1:1.hebrew: וכי תשגו ולא תעשו את כל המצות האלה - וילפינן בהוריות (דף ח.): זו ע"ז, שהיא שקולה ככל המצות; וכתיב: "תורה אחת" — כל התורה במשמע:
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:1:1.english: “And if you err, and do not perform all these commandments” - And we learn in Horayot (8a) [that] this is idolatry, which is equivalent to all the commandments; and it is written: “One law” — the entire Torah is implied.

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:1:2.hebrew: הוקשו - קרבנות של שגגות של כל עבירות לשל ע"ז: מה ע"ז, קרבן שלה אינו בא אלא על עבירה גמורה שחייב על זדונו כרת, דסמיך ליה: "והנפש אשר תעשה ביד רמה", "ונכרתה":
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:1:2.english: They were juxtaposed - The offerings for unwitting [transgressions] of all sins [were juxtaposed] to those of idolatry: Just as [with] idolatry, its offering is brought only for a full transgression for whose intentional [violation] one is liable to karet — for adjacent to it is: “And the person who acts with a high hand,” [and] “shall be cut off.”

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:1:3.english: So too, the entire Torah - One brings a sin-offering only for a matter whose intentional [violation incurs] karet.

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:2:1.hebrew: ואלא מונבז - דאמר לעיל, דמי שהיתה לו ידיעה בשעת מעשה חייב חטאת:
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:2:1.english: However, [according to] Munbaz - Who said earlier that one who had awareness at the time of the act is liable [to bring] a sin-offering:

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:2:2.english: In what was he unwitting - Behold, regarding a sin-offering, "unwittingly" is written.

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:2:3.hebrew: דשגג בקרבן - דיודע שחייב על זדונו כרת, אבל אינו יודע שחייב עליה חטאת:
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:2:3.english: That he was unwitting regarding the sacrifice - That he knows that [one is] liable to karet for its intentional [violation], but he does not know that [one is] liable [to bring] a sin-offering for it:

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:2:4.english: Is not considered unwitting - Unless he was unwitting regarding the transgression itself.

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:3:1.hebrew: ורבנן - דבעו שגגה בעבירה עצמה, שגגה במאי קאמרי: שגגה בכולה מילתא — בלאו וכרת, או בכרת לחודיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:3:1.english: And the Rabbis - Who require inadvertence regarding the transgression itself — regarding what inadvertence do they speak? [Is it] inadvertence regarding the entire matter — regarding [both] the negative commandment and karet — or regarding karet alone?

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:3:2.hebrew: כיון ששגג בכרת אע"ג שהזיד בלאו - שאז הקרבן על הכרת הוא בא, כדאמרן: ״לעושה בשגגה״, וסמיך ליה: ״והנפש אשר תעשה״ וגו':
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:3:2.english: Since he was unwitting with regard to karet, even though he acted intentionally with regard to the negative prohibition - For then the sacrifice comes [to atone] for the karet, as we said: “For one who acts unwittingly,” and juxtaposed to it: “And the person who acts [with a high hand...]”.

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:3:3.english: That may not be done - That is [the] negative prohibition.

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:5:1.hebrew: מנינא למה לי - ליתני: אבות מלאכות — הזורע והחורש כו'. למה לי למיתנא "ארבעים חסר אחת"? ליתנינהו, ואנן ידעינן דמ' חסר אחת איכא:
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:5:1.english: Why do I need the tally? - Let [the mishna] teach: "The primary categories of labor: one who sows, and one who plows," etc. Why do I need [it] to teach "forty-less-one"? Let it teach them, and we would know that there are forty-less-one!

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:5:2.hebrew: שאם עשאן כולן כו' - וסימנא בעלמא אשמעינן, לידע כמה חטאות חייב על חילול שבת אחת:
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:5:2.english: That if he performed all of them, etc. - And [the Mishnah] merely teaches us a mnemonic, to know how many sin-offerings one is liable for on account of the desecration of a single Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:5:3.hebrew: היכי משכחת לה - דמיחייב? ע"כ לא משכחת לה אלא בזדון שבת — דיודע שהוא שבת — ושגגת מלאכות, דאינו יודע שהמלאכות הללו אסורות. דאי בזדון מלאכות ושגגת שבת — דיודע שהן אסורות בשבת, אבל שכח שהיום שבת — הא תנן דאינו חייב אלא אחת לכל שבת. וזדון שבת לא הוי אא"כ יודע אחת מהלכותיה, דאי לא ידע בחדא מינייהו — אין שבת חלוק לו משאר ימים; וזה ששגג בכולן — אין כאן זדון שבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:5:3.english: How can you find it - [That is, under what circumstances is] he liable? Perforce, you cannot find it except in [a case of] intentional [awareness of] Shabbat — where he knows that it is Shabbat — and unwitting [violation of] the labors, where he does not know that these labors are prohibited. For if [it were] in [a case of] intentional labors and unwitting Shabbat — where he knows that they are prohibited on Shabbat, but forgot that today is Shabbat — behold, we learned that he is only liable [to bring] one [sin-offering] for each Shabbat. And intentional [awareness of] Shabbat cannot exist unless he knows [at least] one of its laws, for if he did not know even one of them, Shabbat would not be distinct to him from other days; yet this person, who was unwitting regarding all of them — there is no intentional Shabbat here.

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:6:1.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan - For he said [that] an unwitting [transgression] regarding karet is considered an unwitting [transgression].

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:6:2.hebrew: משכחת לה - זדון שבת בלאוין, ושגגת מלאכות בכריתות — דיודע לה לשבת שהוזהר על הלאוין, או של כולן או של אחת מהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:6:2.english: You find it - [A case of] intentionality regarding Shabbat with regard to negative commandments, and unwittingness regarding the labors with regard to karet: that he is aware of Shabbat, [in] that he was warned regarding the negative commandments — either of all of them, or of one of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:6:3.hebrew: דידע לה לשבת במאי - הלא בכולן שגג, כסבור שכל ל"ט מלאכות מותרות:
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:6:3.english: Through what was he aware of Shabbat? - Did he not err regarding all of them, believing that all thirty-nine labors are permitted?

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:6:4.english: Regarding [Shabbat] boundaries - For they do not entail a sacrifice:

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:6:5.hebrew: ואליבא דר' עקיבא - דאמר במסכת סוטה: תחומין דאורייתא נינהו, דתנן: בו ביום דרש רבי עקיבא: ומדותם מחוץ לעיר כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:6:5.english: And in accordance with Rabbi Akiva - Who said in Tractate Sotah that [Shabbat] boundaries are from the Torah, as we learned: “On that day, Rabbi Akiva expounded: ‘And you shall measure from outside the city...’ etc.”

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:7:1.hebrew: זהו שוגג האמור בתורה - כלומר, היכא דשגג בשבת ובמלאכות, אין כאן לא דין ולא דיין לקנתר, ואין לך שוגג כזה:
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:7:1.english: This is the unwitting [sinner] stated in the Torah - That is to say, where one was unwitting with regard to [both] Shabbat and the [forbidden] labors, there is neither law nor judge to dispute [it], and you have no [greater] unwitting sinner than this.

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:7:2.english: [If] one acted intentionally with regard to both this and that - You have no intentional transgressor like this.

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:7:3.hebrew: שגג באחת מהן - אף זה שוגג, וחייבים עליה קרבן:
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:7:3.english: [If] one acted unwittingly with regard to one of them - This, too, is [considered] an unwitting [transgression], and one is liable to bring a sacrifice for it.

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:8:1.hebrew: שבועת ביטוי - שאוכל ולא אוכל, שאכלתי ולא אכלתי — חייב עליה קרבן, וכתיב ביה "ונעלם", דהיינו שוגג. הכל מודים בשוגג שלה, דאם נשבע "שלא אוכל" ואכל — אינו חייב אלא אם כן שכח שבועתו כשאכל, דהשתא שגג בלאו שבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:8:1.english: An oath on a statement - [Such as:] 'That I will eat' and 'that I will not eat,' 'that I ate' and 'that I did not eat' — [one] is liable to [bring] an offering for it, and it is written concerning it: 'And it is hidden' [from him], which means [that he was] unwitting. Everyone agrees with regard to its unwitting [violation], that if one swore, 'I will not eat,' and he ate, he is not liable unless he forgot his oath when he ate, for then he was unwitting with regard to the prohibition in it.

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:8:2.hebrew: הכל מודים מאן רבי יוחנן - כלומר, על כרחין אביי לאו אפלוגתא דמונבז ורבנן קאי, דלישמעינן דמודה מונבז בהא (דהא) שגגת קרבן לא הויא שגגה — דמהיכא תיתי? והא ק"ו היא: השתא בכל התורה כולה, דליכא חידוש בקרבן דידהו, אמר מונבז דמיחייב בשגגת קרבן; הכא, דחידוש הוא, דאין בה כרת ומביא קרבן עליה — לא כ"ש?! אלא לרבנן קאמר, ואפלוגתא דר"י ור"ל קאי. ומאן "הכל מודים"? ר"י — דאף על גב דבעלמא קאמר אף על פי שהזיד בלאו, הכא בעינן שישגוג בלאו:
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:8:2.english: "Everyone agrees" — who [is this]? Rabbi Yoḥanan - That is to say, perforce Abaye is not referring to the dispute between Munbaz and the Rabbis, to let us hear that Munbaz agrees in this [case] (that) unwittingness regarding an offering is not considered unwittingness — for from where could that be derived? Is it not an a fortiori argument [kal vaḥomer]? Now, in the entire Torah, where there is no novelty in their offering, Munbaz said that one is liable for unwittingness regarding an offering; here, where it is a novelty — for there is no karet in it, yet one brings an offering for it — is it not all the more so?! Rather, he is speaking according to the Rabbis, and he is referring to the dispute of Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish. And who is [meant by] "everyone agrees"? Rabbi Yoḥanan — for even though elsewhere he says [that one is liable] even though he acted intentionally regarding the negative prohibition, here we require that he be unwitting regarding the negative prohibition:

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:8:3.hebrew: פשיטא - כיון דאליבא דרבנן איפליג, דאמרי: שגגת קרבן לאו שגגה היא — אי בלאו שלה הזיד, במאי שגג? דע"כ לא קאמר ר"י בעלמא אלא במקום כרת, דשגג בכרת:
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:8:3.english: It is obvious - Since he disputes [Resh Lakish] according to [the view of] the Rabbis, who say that unawareness of an offering is not [valid] unawareness — if he acted intentionally regarding its negative prohibition, in what was he unwitting? For perforce, Rabbi Yoḥanan only said [so] generally in a case [punishable by] karet, where he was unwitting regarding karet.

Rashi on Shabbat 69a:9:1.hebrew: סלקא דעתך אמינא - בשבועת ביטוי נמי קאי רבי יוחנן במילתיה, דאף על פי שהזיד בלאו. ודקשיא לך: במאי שגג? שגג בקרבן, דהואיל וחידוש, מודו ביה רבנן:
Rashi on Shabbat 69a:9:1.english: It might enter your mind to say - With regard to an oath on a statement as well, Rabbi Yoḥanan stands by his position that [one is liable] even though he acted intentionally regarding the negative prohibition. And as for that which is difficult to you: In what was he unwitting? [He could say that] he was unwitting with regard to the offering, for since [the offering here] is a novelty, the Rabbis concede in this case [to Munbaz].

Tosafot on Shabbat 69a:2:1.hebrew: אלא למונבז שגגה במאי - לא מצי למימר ששגג בלאו והזיד בקרבן, דאין סברא לחייב בהזיד בקרבן, דלא שב מידיעתו הוא. וליכא נמי למימר שגג בלאו וקרבן, דסברא הוא דכיון דמקיש למזיד, אפי' מזיד בכל דבר ושוגג רק בדבר אחד, דהיינו בקרבן, יש לנו לחייבו. ומיהו היכא דאיכא סקילה, בעינן שיהא שוגג גם בסקילה; דאי הוה מזיד בסקילה, אין לחייבו בקרבן, דכיון דאינו שב מסקילה, פשיטא שאפילו היה יודע שחייב גם קרבן שלא היה שב, ולא שב מידיעתו הוא. ואע"ג דבהזיד בכרת חשיב ליה שב מידיעתו לקרבן, היינו משום דכרת אפשר בתשובה, וקרבן לא אפשר בתשובה. ועוד, דגבי כרת שייך שפיר למימר: אם היה יודע שחייב כרת עם הקרבן, היה שב:
Tosafot on Shabbat 69a:2:1.english: However, according to Munbaz, in what was the unawareness - [The Gemara] could not say that he was unwitting regarding the negative prohibition and intentional regarding the sacrifice, because there is no reason to hold [one] liable if he acted intentionally regarding the sacrifice, as he is not one who "turns back upon his awareness." Nor can [the Gemara] say [that he was] unwitting regarding [both] the negative prohibition and the sacrifice, for it stands to reason that since [Munbaz] equates [an unwitting sinner] to an intentional sinner, even if he acted intentionally with regard to everything and was unwitting regarding only one matter — namely, regarding the sacrifice — we should hold him liable. However, where there is [a liability of] stoning, we require that he be unwitting regarding stoning as well; for if he were intentional regarding stoning, he should not be held liable to [bring] a sacrifice, since as he did not turn back from [the threat of] stoning, it is obvious that even had he known that he was also liable to a sacrifice, he would not have turned back, and he is not one who "turns back upon his awareness." And even though when he acted intentionally regarding karet, [Munbaz] considers him one who "turns back upon his awareness" with regard to a sacrifice, that is because karet can be averted through repentance, whereas a sacrifice cannot be averted through repentance. And furthermore, in the case of karet, it is well applicable to say: had he known that he was liable to karet together with the sacrifice, he would have turned back.

Tosafot on Shabbat 69a:2:2.hebrew: כגון ששגג בכרת אע"פ שהזיד בלאו - וטעמא דר' יוחנן משום דלא כתיב לאו בהיקשא דר' יהושע, ולא כתיב אלא כרת בההיא ענינא. ולהכי בעי: "מ"ט דריש לקיש?", ולא בעי מ"ט דר' יוחנן. וצ"ל דרבי יוחנן מיירי אליבא דרבנן, דאית להו היקשא דרבי יהושע בן לוי; אבל לרבי, דנפקא ליה מג"ש דעליה, מודה רבי יוחנן דבעי עד שישגוג בלאו וכרת, דהא כתיב לאו בההוא קרא: "ואשה אל אחותה לא תקח וגו'":
Tosafot on Shabbat 69a:2:2.english: "For example, where he was unwitting regarding karet, even though he was intentional regarding the negative commandment" - And Rabbi Yochanan's reasoning is that a negative commandment is not written in the juxtaposition of Rabbi Yehoshua [ben Levi], and only karet is written in that passage. And that is why [the Gemara] asks: "What is the reason of Reish Lakish?" and does not ask: "What is the reason of Rabbi Yochanan?" And it must be said that Rabbi Yochanan is speaking in accordance with the Rabbis, who accept the juxtaposition of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi; but according to Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi], who derives it from the verbal analogy [gezeirah shavah] of "upon her" [aleha], Rabbi Yochanan concedes that one requires that he be unwitting regarding [both] the negative commandment and karet, as a negative commandment is written in that verse: "And you shall not take a woman to her sister, etc."

Tosafot on Shabbat 69a:3:1.hebrew: אמר קרא אשר לא תעשינה בשגגה - קשה לר"י: מנא ליה לריש לקיש דרבנן דרשי הכי ובעו שגגת לאו? וליכא למימר דמשמע ליה למדרש קרא הכי, דהא ע"כ סבירא ליה דאין סברא לדרוש כן, דהא איהו סבר כמונבז כדאמר לעיל, ומונבז לא בעי שגגת לאו אלא שגגת קרבן גרידא, דבהדיא תניא לקמן: או שאמר: "יודע אני שמלאכה זו אסורה, אבל איני יודע אם חייבים עליה קרבן אם לאו" — חייב, ולא קאמר: "קרבן ומלקות אם לאו":
Tosafot on Shabbat 69a:3:1.english: The verse said: "Which shall not be done in error" - This is difficult to the Ri: From where does Reish Lakish know that the Rabbis expound [the verse] this way and require unawareness of the prohibition? And one cannot say that it made sense to him to expound the verse this way, for he perforce holds that there is no reason to expound [it] like this, since he holds in accordance with Munbaz, as [the Gemara] said earlier, and Munbaz does not require unawareness of the prohibition, but only unawareness of the sacrifice alone. For it is explicitly taught later: Or if he said, "I know that this labor is prohibited, but I do not know whether one is liable to a sacrifice for it or not" — [he is] liable, and it does not say, "[whether one is liable to] a sacrifice and lashes, or not."

Tosafot on Shabbat 69a:6:1.hebrew: דידע לה בתחומין - לא מצי למימר דידע לה בדאיסי, דבההוא נמי חייב חטאת, כדפירשתי בפרק קמא (דף ו: בד"ה הא קמ"ל). תימה לר"י: דאמאי לא קאמר דידע לה לשבת בעשה, דכתיב: "וביום השביעי תשבות וגו'" (שמות כ״ג:י״ב), וכתיב נמי: "ושמרתם את השבת" (שם לא):
Tosafot on Shabbat 69a:6:1.english: That he was aware of it through [the prohibition of Shabbat] boundaries - [The Gemara] could not say that he was aware of it through [the labor mentioned] by Isi [ben Yehuda], for regarding that [labor] as well, one is liable to a sin-offering, as I explained in the first chapter (6b, s.v. Ha kamashma lan). The Ri finds it puzzling: Why did [the Gemara] not say that he was aware of Shabbat through a positive commandment, as it is written: "And on the seventh day you shall rest, etc." (Exodus 23:12), and it is also written: "And you shall keep the Sabbath" (ibid. 31)?

Tosafot on Shabbat 69a:8:1.hebrew: עד שישגוג בלאו שבה - כגון: נשבע שלא יאכל, ואכל, ובשעת אכילה שכח איסור שבועה, וקרינן ביה "האדם" — דבשעת שבועה שנשבע היה יודע היטב איסור שבועה, אלא שבשעת אכילה היה סבור דמותר לעבור על שבועתו. ורש"י פירש, דבשעת אכילה שכח שנשבע. ואין נראה, דאין זה קרוי "שגג בלאו שבה" במה שאינו נזכר שנשבע:
Tosafot on Shabbat 69a:8:1.english: "Until he is unwitting regarding the negative prohibition in it" - For example, [where] one swore that he would not eat, and ate, and at the time of eating he forgot the prohibition of an oath; and we apply to him [the scriptural term] "a man" (Leviticus 5:4) — for at the time of the oath, when he swore, he knew full well the prohibition of an oath, but at the time of eating he thought that it was permitted to violate his oath. And Rashi explained that at the time of eating he forgot that he had sworn. But this does not appear [correct], as this is not called [being] "unwitting regarding the negative prohibition in it" merely by virtue of his not remembering that he had sworn.
